Northside CNRA:
The Northside neighborhood is characterized by single-family residential units. Some concentration of commercial uses occur along 13th Street, a major north/south thoroughfare, and along Taylor Street, a major east/west thoroughfare. Elsewhere in Northside some intersections have commercial businesses on corner lots. Two major city parks and two elementary schools are in the Northside CNRA. Backesto Park, a high-use 10.47 neighborhood park is located between Jackson and Empire Streets, and 13th and 15th Streets. Backesto Park is targeted for significant improvements in the CDBG program. Fred Watson Park is located west of Coyote Creek, east of the adjacent residential area. This 29.30 acre district park is the location of the Northside Community Center constructed during the previous CDBG program and proposed for a small addition in the 1st year of this program. Empire Gardens Elementary School is located at the easterly terminus of Empire Street near Watson Park and Grant Elementary School is on 13th Street just north of Empire.
Olinder CNRA:
The Olinder neighborhood is bordered on the north by one of San Jose's oldest strip commercial areas, East Santa Clara Street. No residential units occur along that frontage. Additional commercial enterprises exist along 24th Street, primarily on the easterly side of the street, outside the project boundary. A further small concentration of commercial occurs in the area of 22nd, 23rd and 24th Streets and William Street. In this area the Western Pacific Railroad line crosses the southeasterly corner of the neighborhood, altering the otherwise residential character of Olinder CNRA.
Olinder is a neighborhood primarily of older residential units, laid out upon the traditional grid street pattern (refer to Urban Design Section). There exist very few units originally designed for multi-family use, and including several larger older homes which have been converted to one-room apartments. The East San Jose Carnegie Library is located at the southeasterly corner of Santa Clara and 24th Streets (refer to the Historical and Archaeological Section). Other institutional uses include the now-vacant site of the Selma Olinder Elementary School at 24th Street, between Santa Clara and San Fernando Streets, and the wooden church located at 20th and San Antonio Streets. The Olinder neighborhood is build-out with little remaining vacant land.
Zoning
Alma CNRA:
The Alma neighborhood is largely residentially zoned, with C-1 zoning along Alma Avenue and M-1 zoning along Monterey Highway and San Jose Avenue. Lots on both sides of Ford Avenue are zoned R-2, multi-family and the remainder of the area is R-1 zoning.
